item.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
item.description: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: From energy crisis to energy transition: How renewables are reshaping energy security
item.description: The continuing conflict in the Middle East is disrupting global energy markets and pushing up fuel prices, with knock-on effects far beyond the region.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan’s farmers are ready to return – private investment could get them there
item.description: The war in Sudan has devastated the economy and agricultural production, but a UN-backed plan aims to mobilise private sector investment to help farmers return to their fields.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: ‘New intensity’ to Russian attacks on Ukraine, Yemen, Gaza and Colombia updates
item.description: Russian armed forces have carried out repeated attacks across Ukraine over the past several days, killing and injuring civilians and damaging homes, hospitals, shops and workplaces, UN human rights monitors said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Guterres calls on countries to set clear timelines for transition away from fossil fuels
item.description: “We are the first generation with the tools to end the fossil fuel age – and the last who can avert climate catastrophe,” UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Wednesday, calling on countries to draw up credible roadmaps with clear timelines to transition away from fossil fuels.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: LIVE: Climate change is here - What happens next is still in our hands
item.description: From deadly floods in the Himalayas to wildfires and extreme heat across Europe, 2026 has brought a succession of stark reminders of a changing climate. The task is immediate: Protect people from the impacts already unfolding while rapidly cutting the emissions of harmful gasses driving climate change. World leaders have been meeting on Wednesday to discuss how to turn those priorities into action.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Less than 4 years from development goals deadline, progress shows what’s possible
item.description: For Benin, making progress on the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has meant finding new ways to finance development.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Money sent home by migrants nearly doubles in a decade
item.description: Migrants sent $728.6 billion home to families in low and middle-income countries in 2025, nearly double the amount recorded a decade earlier, according to a new report from the UN’s International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Countries must increase AI regulation to avoid ‘existential risks’: Türk
item.description: Voluntary self-regulation by companies developing frontier artificial intelligence (AI) is “nowhere near sufficient” to address existing harms and prevent advanced autonomous AI models from circumventing human safeguards, UN human rights chief Volker Türk wrote on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Guterres: Old global order must change as power shifts to emerging economies
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told leaders of a bloc of major emerging economies in New Delhi on Sunday that a more balanced global order requires an overhaul of the institutions built after the Second World War, including the UN Security Council.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN hails Libya election deal as Security Council urges Libyans to seize the moment
item.description: The UN Security Council has welcomed a breakthrough agreement between Libya's rival political blocs, calling it "an important step" towards the country's first national elections in over a decade – while pressing all sides to move quickly from paper to practice.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ships and seafarers increasingly caught in the crossfire of unrelated wars
item.description: The global shipping industry is facing a "genuinely unprecedented" convergence of maritime crises, with vessels and seafarers increasingly used as “leverage” in conflicts that have nothing to do with them.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI datacentres pose growing threat to electricity systems worldwide
item.description: Use of data-intensive technologies – in particular artificial intelligence (AI) data centres – is growing faster than electricity infrastructure can handle, the UN’s economic commission for Europe has warned, raising concerns about the future reliability and resilience of energy systems worldwide.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster
item.description: Amid reports that hundreds of people are still missing in Nepal and China after a floodwater surge slammed into towns and villages on Wednesday, aid teams have been working to reach communities cut off by the disaster.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Red Sea nations step up maritime cooperation as regional threats grow
item.description: From piracy and migrant smuggling to disruptions affecting global shipping routes, countries bordering one of the world’s busiest waterways are seeking closer cooperation to stay ahead of fast-evolving maritime threats.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Protecting our ‘most vital infrastructure’: Pushing back on desertification
item.description: As heatwaves are turning deadlier, fires and disasters are razing cities — and rising seas are erasing territories — one environmental crisis remains dangerously overlooked: the degradation of the land beneath our feet.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: First Person: Syrians lead efforts to clear rubble and rebuild lives
item.description: Communities in Syria are clearing rubble and rebuilding neighbourhoods and livelihoods torn down in the more than a decade of conflict and crisis in the country.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Occupied West Bank: Settler siege of Palestinians marks a new low
item.description: In the occupied West Bank, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, appealed on Thursday to Israeli authorities to help Palestinian families trapped in their homes by settlers for days, amid an intensifying campaign to seize their land.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Deadly attack on Red Sea ship adds to global supply chain uncertainty
item.description: A strike on a merchant ship off the southern coast of Yemen that reportedly killed several seafarers on Tuesday threatens to reignite deep concerns about global trade, amid the ongoing Iran-US war that has choked shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: After post-pandemic improvement, youth unemployment is rising again
item.description: Frustrated by skyrocketing youth unemployment, among other issues, tens of thousands of Gen Z activists took to the streets of Nepal last year, demanding a stake in the country’s economic growth. The protest worked and the prime minister resigned.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Colombia earthquake: UN joins national response
item.description: As earthquake rescue efforts across western Colombia continued on Tuesday, UN agencies said that they stood ready to help “with everything we've got”, in coordination with national authorities.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Food prices edged up in July amid heatwaves and energy price hikes
item.description: The cost of key foods edged up last month as searing heatwaves and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty impacted energy prices around the world.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Strait of Hormuz disruption hits energy, fertilizer and industrial trade
item.description: Disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has exposed the vulnerability of global trade to a single maritime chokepoint, with early data showing sharp falls in exports of energy, fertilizers and industrial products.

item.title: Syria’s hopes for renewal hinge on rebuilding trust, lives and livelihoods
item.description: A country long known as a meeting point of civilizations, Syria stands once again at a crossroads.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Can critical minerals fuel peace and prosperity instead of conflict?
item.description: The Security Council met Wednesday in New York to debate critical minerals — the lithium, cobalt and copper powering the clean energy transition. Demand is set to triple by 2030. The question: will this mineral wealth build peace and prosperity, or fund conflict and corruption? Follow live updates throughout the day below and go here for full coverage from across the UN.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: From lithium to nickel: How the UN is helping countries make the most of critical minerals
item.description: The world's shift to clean energy is driving huge demand for critical minerals such as lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper.

item.title: Critical minerals: The hidden resources powering the clean energy future
item.description: Why are critical minerals suddenly at the centre of global politics?

item.title: As aid dries up, countries pledge to close the $4 trillion development gap
item.description: UN Member States reaffirmed their commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by adopting a declaration on Wednesday that they will implement reforms to help close the $4 trillion SDG financing gap.

item.title: People continue to stand by refugees, Gen Z shows most empathy
item.description: Protection for refugees has been enshrined in international law for more than seven decades, but how much support is there today for those fleeing conflict and persecution?

item.title: Despite hurdles, don’t give up on Sustainable Development Goals, UN urges
item.description: In a world of “parallel realities” where stark inequalities seemingly divide people and challenge the promise of multilateralism, the vision of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is to bring people together and help them achieve a better reality.
